name: Brigand-Veil
specific_features: Automated beacon (distress, navigation, or unknown purpose)
description: Brigand-Veil is a world of water and wrath, banded by storm cells that have raged without interruption since the first survey drones arrived. Between the squalls lie calm emerald reaches where the sea glows faintly blue-green at night, lit by blooms of bioluminescent plankton in numbers found nowhere else. Volcanic rifts seam the ocean floor, occasionally raising new islets that the storms tear down within a decade.

Aboard ship the air tastes of salt and lightning, and sleep comes hard under a sky that grumbles constantly like a distant avalanche. In the calms the silence is worse, broken only by the clicks and songs of leviathan fauna circling below the hull. Rain on the deck plates sounds like applause you did nothing to earn.

The guild charts mark three safe corridors through the Veil, and all three are lies. Wreck-buoys from a dozen navies litter the shallows, yet someone maintains an automated navigation beacon in the heart of the worst storm band, transmitting a code no registered vessel claims. Whoever keeps it running does not want company—or wants exactly the right kind.

Smugglers call the Veil the best insurance in the sector: no patrol hull can survive those storms, but native pilots who read the squall-lines can cross them blindfolded. Hidden anchorage lagoons open behind moving walls of rain, and cargoes vanish there for years. The navy has posted a bounty for the beacon's coordinates; three claimants have collected it posthumously.
